text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000112 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity tier, but the few returned charts support the billed level, so the evidence is mixed.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The panel is genuinely sicker than average, and most 99215s fall on patients with four or more conditions. However, the by-complexity table shows this provider's 99215 share running roughly double the all-provider share in every tier, from 0 conditions through 5+, so patient complexity does not explain the elevation; the risk-adjusted score already accounts for case mix. On the other side, none of the documented 99215 claims were unsupported, and sampled supported notes (e.g., C0062118, C0063278) show high MDM. But only 7 documented 99215 claims from about 3% of all claims is too thin to clear the pattern, and documentation could be templated, since no supported note records minutes. The 99214 unsupported rate (C0062624, C0063430 documented as low MDM) and the 2 data-reviewed notes with no lab line are small, weak signals rather than findings. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215s, especially C0063125 and C0063236 (the same 0-condition patient billed 99215 for J06.9 and a Z09 follow-up) and C0062089, then expand the 99215 records sample to see whether support holds at a larger count."}
